lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They found her in the lower archives district two days after the Collector paid them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The building was half-sunk into the slope above the old flood channel, its upper rooms rented to scribes who couldn't afford better light and its lower rooms left to the kind of people who preferred not to be found. Zeek had come looking for a particular copy of a boundary tablet the Collector had mentioned in passing. BAH-lahg waited outside with the packs. En-HEH-doo had already decided the place smelled like unpaid debts and was keeping one eye on the street.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun was in the back room, seated at a low table covered in clay tablets and scrap parchment. Ink stained both wrists. A small oil lamp burned with the kind of careful thrift that said the oil was more expensive than the work. She looked up when Zeek's shadow crossed the tablets, and for a moment neither of them spoke.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: You're the one who came out of the sealed tomb,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The mark on your hand matches a symbol that appears on seven private royal seals and nowhere else in the public record. The same symbol that shows up in the oldest underworld fragments the temple pretends not to keep. I've been looking for someone who actually saw it in the ground instead of on a tablet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg's bulk filled the doorway behind Zeek. He didn't speak, but the way he stood said he had already decided this woman was either useful or a problem.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo drifted in last, eyes moving over the tablets, the lamp, the ink-stained hands.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun looked at each of them in turn.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Someone who spent three years watching a district rearrange itself around my sister until the city records forgot she had ever lived there. Someone who is finished being told the old texts are only metaphor.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The room went quiet except for the small hiss of the lamp.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: People often rushed to fill silence.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: That interested him more than anything she'd said so far.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun reached beneath one of the stacked tablets and produced a narrow wooden board wrapped in faded linen.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She hesitated only long enough to brush dust from it before laying it carefully on the table.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Inside rested seven clay impressions, each no larger than a man's thumb.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun pointed to the first impression.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Her finger moved to the next.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: This one was catalogued as belonging to his grandson.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: At first glance the spirals appeared identical.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then he noticed the tiny variations.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He looked farther along the line.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg looked from one to the other.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I feel like I'm listening to two people discuss sheep.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: This symbol appears nowhere before this reign.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Finally she touched the last impression.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek's eyes remained fixed on the clay.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: But the kings are still there.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: I've spent four years copying tablets that no longer agree with tablets copied twenty years earlier.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Kings don't allow the same mistake on three hundred different tablets.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She reached beneath the table again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: This time she produced a broken fragment no larger than her palm.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The temple archives catalogued this as an inventory.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The reverse side carried faint scratches.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She smiled for the first time.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: …unless I've been following exactly the same trail as your father.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek felt the mark under the linen give a single, slow pulse. He ignored it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: I'm not asking to be hired.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun stood. She was shorter than En-HEH-doo and carried herself like someone who had learned to take up less space than she needed.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: I'm telling you I already know more about the symbol on your skin than the Collector does, and I am coming with you whether you like the arrangement or not.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg made a low sound that might have been a laugh.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo tilted her head, studying her the way she studied anything that might turn out to have unexpected value.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: I don't care about the silver.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: I care about the tablets that keep going blank. I care about the streets that only exist when the fog is thick enough. I care about the fact that my sister's name no longer appears in any record the city is willing to admit exists.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun's voice stayed level, but something underneath it had gone hard.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: You can keep the silver. I want the truth the city is trying to edit out of itself.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked at her for a long moment.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He thought of the wet ink in his father's journal. The compass that pointed straight down. The way the Collector had already known more than he should. He thought of the empty space where KOO-rash had walked and the way the desert had already started forgetting the boy's footprints.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: You slow us down, we leave you,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: You get us killed chasing blank tablets, I'll make sure the city remembers your name long enough to regret it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun almost smiled. It didn't reach her eyes.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked at En-HEH-doo. She gave the smallest shrug, the kind that said she had already calculated the risk and decided it was acceptable for now.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Pack light. We leave at first light. And if the Collector asks, you were never here.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Outside, the lower district continued its ordinary noise—scribes arguing, a donkey complaining, someone shouting about a missing delivery. The city had not yet noticed the fourth share being added.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek flexed his left hand inside the linen and started walking.
